utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Misetic, is the Gotovina Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Madam Usher. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: There is one issue -- actually, two issues I think we'd like to raise before the witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What's the issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: One, my colleague Mr. Hedaraly is going to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you -- your so new that you're still the unidentified speaker.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, it's Carrier, C-a-r-r-i-e-r.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you will get your reputation soon, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: One of the issues is Mr. Misetic contacted us and Asked whether we had any objections to adding two documents to their 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I can indicate that the first document which is memo from Mr. Jarnjak, or Minister Jarnjak, I have no issue with that. That was actually, I believe, on the Cermak Defence 65 ter list, which is 65 ter 2D00-531. The other document is a table, and on the Cermak Defence 65 ter list it's 65 ter 2D00-131. The problem that we're having with this is that it's a table -- it's not clear what the provenance of the table is. Moreover, there a number of different tables included in the initial group of documents that was sent to the OTP by Mr. Misetic, not all of them have been translated. There is also a three-page document that was initially included that had -- that has not been translates so we don't know exactly what that consists of. My understanding is that this was actually -- both of these documents, one that we're not objecting to, and the other one were shown to the next witness during the proofing session, although my understanding is that initially when it was shown to him it was shown to him as -- as though it was an attachment to the first document which we don't have any issue with. Which the Prosecution understands is not the case, that these are actually separate documents. I think Mr. Misetic is now clear these are actually two separate documents. We just don't know where the send one came from, who created it, for what purpose, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber has been copied on a short e-mail message on which you announced that you would seek to have admitted documents to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently the first one which - this was said by Mr. Carrier - is on the, I think, on the Cermak 65 ter list, that that seems, therefore, not to be a major problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: They both are on the Cermak 65 ter list. However, the reason we have them as one document is because when they were produced to us, if the Chamber looks at the original of what we sent, both documents were together in one file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And the first page of the B/C/S shows the file marking on it, and in the original says that the file is called Separate Police Units, and OA Povratak is in the upper right-hand corner. So when they were produced to us, they were produced to us as one file. The second point, Mr. President, is that this witness in fact was part of the OA Povratak operational command. The document that Mr. Carrier is referencing, the table, is titled OA Povratak. It's part of OA Povratak and would have been clearly a table prepared as part of OA Povratak of which this witness was a member of the operational command as -- in his position as assistant minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must, admit reading it on my screen, I have to turn my head 180 degrees. So it was presented as one document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: One file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One file.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that in any way -- this explanation, does that in any way meet your concerns, Mr. Carrier? UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: Some additional information, Mr. President, is a that we have received the initial document from Minister Jarnjak, I think, on a number of occasions always as a separate document, not part of a file. I understand my friend's position that this witness is part of the OA Povratak command, although in his statement he doesn't actually indicate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in his statement, of course, this is not a 92 ter witness for --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There is a 92 ter motion that was filed, last Thursday, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Last Thursday, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Or Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have the statement, so don't worry about that. But I thought that -- yes. Yes, therefore, when I intervened when you referred to the statement was incorrect. Mr. Carrier, please proceed where I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Just following up on that, we don't have any objection to the statement under 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Despite what Mr. Misetic says about Mr. Zidovec being part of the OA Povratak command, he doesn't indicate that in his statement. It's just not clear where this table's come from. But, moreover, there's also a number of things that haven't been translated with regard to that file, just as portions, so we don't have actually the whole file at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as translation are concerned, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that. I wasn't aware that all of it wasn't translated, although I see that most of it is information that I don't think needs to be translated, but if the headers are not translated, we'll be sure to correct that. But let me also point out that at paragraph 30 of the witness's statement concerning his participation in the OA Povratak command, he says all assistants to the minister were part of Povratak, insofar as their areas of responsibilities were engaged in that operation. So he as an assistant minister, Mr. President, we would submit was in fact part of Povratak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now let's try to find a very practical solution. Mr. Misetic would like to have this document added to the 65 ter list. Id there any way that you introduce the document without showing it to the witness asking him question? I take it that you have gone through the document during the proofing sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you -- if you ask questions about have you seen a document; or were you shown a document of this and this kind; could you explain to us whether this was what it was; et cetera. So the 65 ter list is there to make sure that the other party knows in advance what will be put to the witness. Now, apparently here it is not that there is it some fundamental objection against adding this one, but that there are still some questions in relation to that, where does it come from, et cetera et cetera. Of course, without showing the document yet, we could seek to clarify some of the issues Mr. Carrier raised. Was it -- you say it is one file. Mr. Carrier seems not to know whether it was one file, what is the relation between the one document and the other. If you start with the one and say, Was anything attached to it; or did you see any document related to it; and what do you know about that document? And then make your oral application to have it added to the 65 ter list, because Mr. Carrier will be better in a position to respond to that oral application in relation to the second document. Do you understand what I mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President. I can just tell you that in the proofing the witness, he doesn't -- and I think as is evident, made perhaps from his statement, he doesn't have very specific recollections of specific documents. The first document noted that it was sent to all assistant ministers of the interior, from which the witness confirms that in the ordinary course of business he would have received a copy of if it, if in fact it says that it went to all assistant ministers of the interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness doesn't know that much about it, have you then considered to tender it as a bar table exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would, Mr. President. I would just say that if possible I would avoid that only because this is -- we would submit a document that -- at least the first document would have gone to him as a recipient of the document, so there is no need to bar table it. If there is an issue regarding whether that was part of the file or not, then we'll bar table the second one. But I would also add that given that he in paragraph 30 of his statement says that he in fact was part -- or engaged in OA Povratak as an assistant minister, we think that adds something in terms of his basis of knowledge to comment on the general statistics of how many police may have been engaged in the area. And I would note that on that specific question, at paragraph 36 of his statement, the OTP asked him questions on deployment of police, specifically, the separate police units which is in fact the file folder that I'm now trying to tender, is the statistics on the separate police units that were deployed. So in fact the Prosecution -- but for the Prosecution having flagged this for us in their statement of the witness, we perhaps wouldn't have even looked there. So the file folder actually is simply adding to what the witness is already going to testify to as to paragraph 36 of his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at paragraph 31 of his statement he actually says: "I did not directly participate in the operation," in relation to operation Povratak. And again, the issue with the table as opposed to the document from Minister Jarnjak is, the one from Minister Jarnjak we agree is sent directly to all assistant ministers, whereas the table isn't, which is the issue. And we -- they're not connected in any way or at least not in a way that is obvious to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may at one point. Perhaps, if it is going to be an issue as to whether he was part of Povratak or not, I think the Prosecution is aware that the witness issued many orders during and after Operation Storm. And in the upper right-hand corner coded them as being part of OA Povratak. So I will take him through those, his own orders, under OA Povratak if that is an issue, but I don't think it should be in dispute even -- that the witness participated in OA Povratak.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And we don't dispute that he was part of it. It's just that he says he was, and so it's just not clear what he would have been receiving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no dispute that he was, but he is saying that he was not part of it, of the operation or whether he -- Let's -- if you can't resolve the matter, if the objection against this part of the document to be admitted -- to be added to the 65 ter list stands, then, of course, the Chamber will have to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, the Chamber invites you to make the oral application to add it to the 65 ter list at the best possible moment before the break, when the -- when you think you have laid the ground-work as good as you can, and we'll then decide during the break having a closer at the document and translations, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So and the first one is -- leave is granted to add the -- the first one, there was no objection, Mr. Carrier. So leave is granted for that one, and the other one we'll hear from you when we are in a best position to decide on the matter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. President, with respect to the discussion last week, let me just advise the Chamber that with respect to expert reports, Mr. Jones's report will be available by 9.00 a.m. on Thursday. With respect to Mr. Pokaz's report, we have now engaged three translators to get that done by Thursday at 9.00 a.m. as well, and that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were invited to tell us what portion was already translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First 15 pages have been translate by Friday, but there was a significant amount that was left, and we had to engage other interpreter/translators to get that done. So we have hired -- or engaged two additional translators, who are now working on separate sections of the document. A draft translation will be completed by Thursday at 9.00 a.m. Obviously, we will then work on a final translation after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not going to be asking Mr. Hedaraly or Mr. Carrier whether you're happy with it, but whether you can live with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We'll live with it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. I spoke too quickly. I was not going ask you whether you were happy with it. And since that word does not appear too often on the transcript, it would be a pity if it would miss it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, let me just also note that while the witness is coming in that there were three documents that had an ERN number, ERN number, in the statement which have not yet been admitted into evidence. They are all in the Prosecution's -- all three are on the Prosecution's 65 ter list. I've had a conversation with Mr. Carrier and Mr. Hedaraly, and at the conclusion of the 92 ter, I would like to simply move those 65 ter exhibits into evidence so that the statement is complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll proceed as suggested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zidovec. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration at the beginning of your testimony, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher, and I would like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zidovec. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, you will first be examined by Mr. Misetic. Mr. Misetic is counsel for Mr. Gotovina. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zidovec.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can extra microphones please be turned off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, could you please state your full name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: My name is Zdravko Zidovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, I would like to turn your attention to a statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2007. It is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar 65 ter, 1D27-68. If we could have that on the screen, please. And, Madam Usher, if you would assist me in providing a hard copy in B/C/S to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, if you look at the screen first, on the left-hand side is the original English statement that has some signatures on the bottom. Do you recall whether your signature is on the first page of this statement? Can you tell us whether it is?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: I recognise it. This is the text of the statement I gave to the investigators in June of 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Zidovec, yesterday you pointed out to us two areas that you wanted to address, if we could turn your attention to paragraph 55 of your statement, please. Is there anything you wish to correct in paragraph 55 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to make a correction. The figure I gave at the time, which has to do with the list of between 1200 and 1300 bodies throughout the territory covered by Operation Storm, that the units of the civilian protection sanitized in the course of August and thereafter. The figure, unfortunately, was not correct. The number involved is 902 bodies that the civilian protection sanitized throughout the area of its activity as part of operation Povratak in the wake of Operation Storm covering the stretch from Sisak to the area covered by the Split-Dalmatia police administration. The error was made due to the fact that I had a very short period of time at my disposal to prepare for my discussions with investigators, and in that short period I did not have occasion to obtain documents that would allow me to recall the exact figures. The reason why I was unable to get the documentation was that, as of 2001, when the civilian protection became part of the state administration for rescuing, that particular documentation relating to the civil protection had been archived in the state archive and was no longer accessible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that if Mr. Misetic would be interested to know all the backgrounds, why you said what you said at the time, and why you could not have said otherwise, and then he will certainly ask for it. If you just make the correction needed, and maybe that there are questions, you'll then hear about it. But let's first try to keep focussed on what, apparently, Mr. Misetic is seeking, to have a correction on a number. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. And let me just -- I don't think this is going to be disputed, Mr. President, by the Prosecution, so let me just save some time by saying --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, at paragraph 58 in the Croatian version of this document it says that -- the report says that there was a dispatch of 100 conscripts to Gracac fire station. In the original English, it says that the dispatch was of 20 conscripts to the Gracac fire station, and so there's a correction that needs to be made in your -- translated version. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Other than -- other than these two corrections, is there anything else in your 2007 witness statement to the Prosecution that needs to be corrected?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to make another correction which was the result again of an error on my part, and this is the mention of -- or, rather, in paragraph 13 and 15 of the B/C/S version of the Croatian version of my statement, I talked about the preparation of the civilian protection for the protection of civilians against any harm that may come to them, not in the course of the Operation Storm, but in the course of another operation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last part of what you said. You said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It had to do with the preparations of the civilian protection for the evacuation of the population for possible enemy operations in the course of Ljeto, Summer 95, the order to that effect came from the office for defence of the country of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is there anything else that needs to be corrected in your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: I think that the other paragraphs reflect our discussions more or less, and I would have no other interventions to make at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, is there a problem with the transcripts in LiveNote? I see that the LiveNote is working on the main monitors but not on the individual stations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wasn't looking at the other screen, but I see that it's stopped at page 12, line 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since it seems to be operational on the other screen, I suggest that we proceed, because that means that from a technical perspective, that there is a reliable transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which certainly, sooner or later will appear on our personal screens as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, your 2007 statement, with the -- excluding the corrections that have you now made, does the statement accurately reflect what you said to investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: It does, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At the time you gave this statement in 2007 to investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor, did you give the statement to the best of your knowledge and in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: I confirm that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, if I asked you the same questions today that you were asked in 2007, would your answers be the same today as they were in 2007 and as reflected in your 2007 witness statement, subject to your clarifications?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: They would be the same, of course. Although they would be substantiated by better figures and facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask -- that 65 ter 1D27-68 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit D1570.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have, Mr. President, explained the process of reading a witness summary to the witness. And with your permission and leave, I would like to read out the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness Zdravko Zidovec was the assistant minister of the interior during and after Operation Storm, responsible for information, analysis, and fire and civil protection. The witness states that his preparation for Operation Storm began only a few days before the operation. The witness was responsible for the establishment of reception centres for civilians after Operation Storm. There was no plan to bring to the reception centres those persons who were capable of living by themselves. The witness was also responsible for the burial of human remains after Operation Storm. The task of collecting bodies was within the exclusive authority of the civil protection. In the event that a body was found by the civil protection where the cause of death appeared to be suspicious, the responsibility for criminal investigation was with the crime police of the Ministry of Interior. A crime technician of the crime police would accompany the civil protection unit at every burial. In the aftermath of Operation Storm, the witness states that the civil protection units searched 48.000 houses in the liberated areas, primarily for the purposes of sanitation. Than concludes the witness summary, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, now with your leave I would like to tender into evidence three documents mentioned in the witness's 92 ter statement. The first document is referenced at paragraph 53 of the statement. It is ERN number 0607-5489, which is 65 ter 4664. I'd like to move that into evidence. The second document is referenced at paragraph 58 of the statement. It is ERN number 0349-3739, and it is 65 ter 4440. And the third document is referenced at paragraph 70 of the statement. It is ERN number 0349-3704, and it is 65 ter 4430. And I'd ask that the three exhibits be marked, and I tender them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, 4664.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 4664 becomes Exhibit D1571. 65 ter 4440 becomes Exhibit D1572. And 65 ter number 44330 becomes Exhibit D1573.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1571 through D1573 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if we could have on the screen, please, Exhibit P-- that's P1148, please. And if we could go to English page 5 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, you were responsible for the civil defence, and I'd first like to show you by way of background the Law on Amendments to the Law on Internal Affairs. This is beginning at Article 24 -- sorry. 24b. Now -- it's page 4 of the B/C/S. Now, Mr. Zidovec, could you tell us what this law is, in relation to the work of the civil defence. How this law relates to the work of the civil defence.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Civilian protection came under the competence of the Ministry of Interior in January of 1994, alongside fire-fighters and some other activities, because it had been shown that the Law on -- in the interior had to be amended. This particular provision fully covers the activities of civil protection; namely, protection and rescue of citizens and properties, as well as dealing with consequences of natural disasters, technological and environmental disasters. What was also envisaged were the consequences of nuclear disasters, as well as, of course, war activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Zidovec, I would like now like to turn your attention -- turning directly to Operation Storm, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we could turn to Exhibit D232, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is an order of yours from the 4th of August to all police administrations. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You'll see that this is the order activating the civil protection and the fire service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 2 of this document in the English and leave it on page 1 in the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you look at paragraph 3, you order that in the police administrations, including Zadar-Knin and Sibenik: "Immediately prepare the activation of civil protection units," and then underlined: "Immediately activate a detachment for hygiene and sanitation members [sic] and a detachment for terrain clearing ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And then in the next paragraph, if we could turn the page in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says that: "The police administrations, in cooperation with the military authorities, and on their approval engage in the removal of the bodies of the dead in cooperation with the criminal police." Now, first, can you explain to the Chamber what you meant when you said that the police administrations are to remove bodies of the dead in cooperation with the military authorities?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: This part of the sentence relates to a very clear form of cooperation, which had previously been defined in the removal of bodies. The crime investigation police, i.e., forensic officers who normally conduct scene-of-crime investigations had to be part and parcel of the team involved in the removal of bodies. This meant that the forensic officer was supposed to attend the scene where the body was found and take all the steps prescribed by the law, i.e., examine the body, collect all information that may help in the identification of the body, such as lifting finger-prints. What also had to be examined was the manner in which the person died possibly, the body had to be photographed, and, finally, what had to be produced was a detailed crime report or detailed forensic report. It was only once the forensic officer conducted his examination was the civilian protection allowed to proceed to bury the remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'll get back to it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What I would like to tell everyone is that the system is functioning apparently again and that you have to reconnect to the server to receive the running LiveNote on your personal screen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, this process of having a crime investigator do an investigation prior to the burial, would that also include bodies of ARSK soldiers that may have been encountered? In other words, did the MUP civil protection units also bury bodies of ARSK soldiers, and, if so, would the MUP crime investigator also do the same process of photographing the body, producing a detailed crime report, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, going back to -- to paragraph 4, can you explain a little bit further what you meant when you said that this was to be done in cooperation with the military authorities. What did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: This meant primarily that communication had to take place as to whether civilian protection teams could be dispatched to specific areas where it was known that the remains of those killed were to be found, and where no direct combat activities had taken place. Secondly, it also meant that we counted on the possible assistance of military machinery, in order to prepare the burial sites, in keeping with the conventions that we were duty-bound to adhere to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Zidovec, let me turn your attention now to Exhibit D233. And in paragraph 64 of your statement, you say that: "Only civil protection had the task of collecting bodies. This authority belonged exclusively to the civil protection." Now, this is an order of yours from the 5th of August.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And here you have laid out a procedure for the burial of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me wait for the Croatian version to be on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before my friend continues, if he could ask perhaps what the procedure was, rather than reading out the order. It's leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think the witness just testified what the procedure was, the photographing, the bodies, et cetera. There is already foundation. There is foundation in the statement, and it's the witness's own document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even the question was put whether that covered also ARSK soldiers found, if that is the procedure. But I haven't, of course, looked at the document yet, whether this document describes a different procedure or whether it just gives the details. Mr. Carrier, Mr. Misetic responded to your objection. Does that change your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: No, because he was starting off saying -- referring to the document saying you lay out the procedure. And then I just wanted to make -- I was clarifying whether or not he intended just to read it him, or if he could ask him what the procedure was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But Mr. Misetic answered that he had asked already about the procedure and that only after that he now draws the attention of the witness to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And this one goes into more detail, I suppose is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I may also add that at paragraph 46 of the witness's statement, this exhibit specifically was shown to him. He commented on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances, please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, as I said at paragraph 46, you referenced that you were shown this document by the Prosecution. This is -- can you explain to the Chamber what this document was, why you issued this order.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: The document was issued one day after the start of Operation Storm. We were certainly expecting civilian victims as well as military victims in the area. For this reason, we issued a document where we defined in detail for the relevant police administrations the procedure that they had to follow in applying hygiene and sanitation measures. We believed that such a set of instructions was very important because it was the civilian protection units from these very police administrations that were the first to reach the area. We wanted to make sure that no omissions or errors are made in developing documentation and burying remains. We thought it important to draw their attention to these matters once more, and, in particular, I refer to item 4, where, in very precise terms, we describe the manner of burial that needed to be followed for every body.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Zidovec, let me turn your attention to Exhibit P898, and you reference this document that we're -- I'm about to show you at paragraph 54 of your statement. First, can you tell the Chamber who Slavko Maric was during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Slavko Maric was the head of the forensic centre at the crime police at the seat of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you were shown this document by the Prosecution, and it talks about the identification of persons and dead bodies -- procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we turn to page 2 in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, you have already testified in court about photographing bodies, et cetera. Is the section under the portion that -- titled "Dead Bodies" is this the procedure, as you understood it, of what was to be done?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, can you explain from the perspective of the MUP what the process of photographing a body might mean in an investigation? In other words -- let me be more specific. Does photographing a body begin an investigation? What is it procedurally within the Ministry of Interior when a body is photographed?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: I believe that this is one of the key activities of the police. In this particular case, it was simply necessary to make photographs, in order, first of all, to be able to prove the condition of the body when found. Also, whether there were any visible marks which could help the experts as to why this particular person died.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, let me turn your attention to Exhibit D1571. This is referenced at paragraph 53 of your statement. And in your statement at paragraph 53, you say what we're about to see on the screen: "... is an instruction sent by me, dated 6 August 1995, with an example of the form that was to be filled out by the sanitation group."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please. And I believe one more page in the English to get to the attachment. If we ... Can we also turn the page in the Croatian version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, is this the form that the civil protection units were supposed to use when registering bodies that were found?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, you see the columns there, and there's a number, identification number; and then status, civilian or soldier. Could you tell the Court first how the status of the person would be determined.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: The fundamental element was obviously the equipment or parts of uniform that was -- that were found on the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, if I could turn your attention to Exhibit D69, please. Now, this is the OA Povratak list of individuals at the end that were all collected. Was this -- comparing your previous form that you had sent out with the final Povratak list of bodies, can you confirm that this list was prepared pursuant to the instruction that you had sent on the 6th of August?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zidovec, I'd like to turn briefly to the issue of the HV and sanitation, and this is related to paragraphs 65 through 69 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we could first turn to Exhibit D598, please. It is an order of General Cervenko from the 5th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The order, in point 1, says that the Military Districts are to establish mixed sanitation detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we could turn the page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, the paragraph above, numbered paragraph 2 in General Cervenko order it says: "In establishing the detachment, ensure that the sanitation teams invariably include criminal investigation technicians from MUP for identification, persons for keeping records, medical team ..." et cetera. And if I could turn your attention to Exhibit D234, please. This is General Cervenko's order on the 5th. This is now a document which reflects the minutes of a meeting held on the 6th of August between the heads of the crime investigation departments in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we turn the page in English, please. And turn the page in Croatian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, the sentence above the section that begins AD-2, it says: "Mr. Zidovec liaises with the HV regarding hygiene and sanitation measures and the identification." Now can you tell the Chamber whether you recall liaising with the HV concerning sanitation measures?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Given the situation which the first civil protection units encountered in the field on the 5th of August, we thought that it was necessary to come by logistical support, i.e., mechanisation that would enable us to carry out sanitation, that is removal of the bodies as quickly as possible, the bodies that were found in the ground. The civilian protection did not have any such mechanisation. And that I believe that in the crime police department, they were also convinced that such mechanisation could be achieved through a cooperation with the Croatian Army. I am not aware of any specific arrangements made in the field, but I do know that this document came to me, it was submitted to me. And as regards making the necessary mechanisation available, it was done on the ground, arranged by our representatives who were there and most probably the military authorities that were also there. If I may go back to the order of General Cervenko, which I was just shown, I would like to say once again that, according to all my knowledge, the sanitation of human bodies was carried out exclusively by civilian protection, in cooperation with crime police, and this was done in the way which I previously described. Certain other elements of this order by General Cervenko indicate that there was -- that we were supposed to set up a rather -- or to have a rather ideal situation in order to be able to carry out this order, but we were far from any such ideal situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if could I have exhibit 65 ter 1D830, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, this is also a document of yours dated 6 August 1995. And you appointed Mr. Boris Davidovic as the deputy head -- who was the deputy head of the MUP civilian protection as coordinator for clearing the terrain of bodies. And you sent this to the Zadar-Knin police administration operative staff. Do you recall appointing Mr. Davidovic in the field to coordinate the collection of bodies?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you look in the upper right-hand corner of this document, it says OA Povratak. Can you tell the Chamber why you issued this document with those words on the page?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: This was done because all of the affairs as of the morning of the 4th of August and also in the case that we had in May of that year during the Operation Flash, all that was done within the framework of the OA Povratak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were you, as an assistant minister, part of OA Povratak?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, because of the duties that I carried out at the time. All assistant ministers and all the work carried out at the time belonged to the operational action Povratak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that 65 ter 1D830 be marked, and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit D1574.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could have Exhibit D43 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, this is a document dated 7 August 1995 bearing your signature and stamp. And it says: "Assistance to the Zadar-Knin police administration." And then it says: "For the needs of rapid terrain clearance of the town of Knin, urgently mobilize 100 civilian protection conscripts from the area of Sinj. The unit shall be dispatched for jobs relating to the clearing of the terrain and roads in the area of town of Knin." "The unit must report to Mr. Stanko Batur at the Knin police station." Can you tell the Chamber who Mr. Stanko Batur was.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanko Batur was chief of section of the civilian protection at the police administration in Zadar, and immediately after the completion of the Operation Storm he was sent to Knin because the then police in Knin simply had nobody who would be capable to take over the duties, which according to the first information received, were supposed to be very abundant. On the 5th of August, the chief of Department of the Civilian Protection from the ministry arrived to Knin along with his associates. They estimated the situation pertaining to the civilian protection activities, and this was the main reason why we requested from the nearest police administration to provide such a number of persons. They mostly were supposed to engage in cleaning of the town, following the combat activities, and what particularly concerned us at the time was an estimate that in a large number -- that the large number of houses and apartments were abandoned. And in order to prevent any possibly socially critical element we were supposed to act.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We will get that topic in a few minutes, Mr. Zidovec. But I just wanted to establish who Mr. Batur and Mr. Davidovic were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if we could now have exhibit 65 ter D1837, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court briefly to Damir Cemerin was.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Damir Cemerin was chief of Department of Civilian Protection at the seat of the ministry which belonged to the section for fire services and civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a document from Mr. Cemerin to you on the 11th of August, reporting on the state of civilian protection activities in the Zadar-Knin and Lika-Sinj police administrations. And it was reported to you that: "On 11 August at 0800 hours a meeting was held with Mr. Cetina; Mr. Djurica; Mr. Batur, who we just spoke about; Mr. Davidovic was also present at the meeting. And if we go to the third paragraph, it saw says Mr. Batur and Vanjak reported that activities were proceeding with relative difficulty because of the large area and the lack of logistic support partly within the police administrations, but above all, from the bodies in the canton. "They also reported on a meeting with representatives of the Croatian army who had committed themselves to joining in the clearing the area and with all available means, and above all, in burying animals and collecting and caring for animals which are mainly roaming around the liberated territory. To carry out that commitment the Croatian army would join the action after 12 August with three to four excavators, lorries, and about 150 soldiers, as well as hygiene teams and units for the combat security of the areas where the teams are working." Now, is this a report that you received on or about the 11th of August, from Mr. Cemerin?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will ask you a few questions about this document after we look at the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But, in the interim, Mr. President, I tender 65 ter 1D837 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D1575.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, this document talks about lack of logistic support and what the Croatian army had agreed to do on -- on or about the 11th of August. And, Mr. Zidovec, let's turn to Exhibit P496, please. What I'm going to show you is an order of General Gotovina from that same day, 11 August.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And now it talks about -- it makes a reference to General Cervenko's initial order. And in the aim of clearing up the terrain, point 1 is the establishment of a mixed detachment. And if we look at paragraph 3, of this, if you look at the entries at number 2 and number 3, General Gotovina's order makes reference to Mr. Davidovic and Mr. Batur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether or not Mr. Misetic is going read this document to him our ask him whether he knows anything about it, or whether he has seen it before, whether he was aware of it at the time. It seems to be leading if you just read it out to him without any foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we do not know yet what the questions will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just ten minutes going over who Boris Davidovic and Stanko Batur are. I haven't had a chance to even ask the question yet. So there are plenty of foundation laid for this witness knowing who those individuals are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which does not necessarily include his knowledge of this document, but you may proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, you see that two of the people from the MUP are included in an order of General Gotovina. First of all, can you tell us, based on your knowledge as assistant minister, could General Gotovina order Boris Davidovic or Stanko Batur?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: No, I do not have any such knowledge, and I cannot confirm that this was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, it's not for the first time that have I difficulties in understanding the answer. The question was: "Could General Gotovina order Boris Davidovic or Stanko Batur." The answer is: "No, I do not have any such knowledge and cannot confirm that this was the case." Did you want to say that General Gotovina could not give any orders to Boris Davidovic and Stanko Batur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no specific knowledge. I cannot at all recall that the three persons listed here who belonged to the civilian protection received any orders directly from General Gotovina, or they -- indeed, that they carried out these orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that wasn't the question. The question was whether General Gotovina was in a position to give orders to these persons. That was the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think he was in a position to do so. But let me just add that there was no need for such order, since the civilian protection had very specific --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether there was any need for anything was, again, not the question. There are, I would say, three options. The first one is he could; the second one is he could not; and the third one is I do not know. If he could, I think that Mr. Misetic will further explore on what basis; if could not, Mr. Misetic or Mr. Carrier, at a later stage, will explore the basis for such an answer. If you don't know, then we are informed about that. Could we try to keep our answers as clear as possible. And, Mr. Misetic, in this context, if you would not mind, otherwise we would have waited for a second. But if I take to you page 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My LiveNote is now down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your LiveNote is down. Oh, I will read the -- and perhaps the witness could listen with me as well. You said in one of your answers that, when we're talking about number of persons, you would need, you said, What particular concerned us at the time was an estimate, that in a large number, that the large number of houses an apartments were abandoned and -- I'm specifically focussing on the last part of your answer which reads: "And in order to prevent any possibly socially critical element, we were supposed to act." I've got no idea --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President let me just state --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I've got a whole section to go into this issue, but if you wish to clarify that sentence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But, for me, it's -- if I would unkind, I would describe it as bureaucratic language, very much vague and not very to the point. So I would like to invite you to give answers as clear as possible and as factual as possible. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, turning to this order, at page 25, line 15, of today's transcript, you talk about - I'm sorry, but my LiveNote has now crashed - a necessity to come by logistics, mechanisation, et cetera, to enable us to carry out sanitation and removal of bodies as quickly as possible. Are you aware of whether the Split Military District was providing logistics to the civil defence to assist it in removing bodies and fulfilling its civil protection tasks?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, noting your admonition about prior to the break, let me turn to that topic right now. Although, Mr. President, let me ask a procedural question. I'm reminded that the two documents are on the Cermak Defence 65 ter exhibit list. Am I allowed to use documents that are on their list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, in view of the function of 65 ter lists, would you object against the use of the documents which appear on the exhibit list of another party?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: In this circumstance I'm not opposed to the Gotovina Defence adding it to their 65 ter list. But my objection was more about whether or not this person can obviously speak to the specific part of the -- one of the documents. That is something I can raise at the point it is, perhaps, specifically addressed depending on the foundation, but that was a long way of saying no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Until now, I think the only thing we discussed was an application to add the documents to the 65 ter list, and their appears now to be no objection to that, which would have saved us a bit of time earlier. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted to add the documents to your 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, as assistant minister of the defence -- sorry, and an assistant minister of the interior, would you regularly receive copies of instructions or orders from the Minister of the Interior that would be sent to all ministers -- all assistant ministers of the interior?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: I think I can answer the question in the affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Turning your attention to paragraph 36 of your statement, you were asked questions about groups of 100 separate police being sent to the various police administrations to carry out difficult duties. "I believe these groups were formed as additional control over the territory to assist in controlling the movement of people and groups in the area, in particular, they were to form check-points to execute this task of controlling movement." How do you -- what is your basis of knowledge about the sending in of groups of police officers and the reasons why these additional officers were sent in the area?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: I know about it because the OA Povratak staff constantly received information about the uncontrolled movement of various individuals of different status. There was a large presence of the army there, a large presence of refugees and returnees. The need arose for such check-points to be erected in the area, in order to maintain public law and order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Would have you received information -- as part of this information, would you have also received copies of reports about the numbers of police that were being sent in and withdrawn from the liberated areas?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: I suppose that this was the case, but I cannot confirm that it happened in every case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, on this basis, may I show him the documents or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, let me show 2D00-531, please. Now, this is again a part of OA Povratak, and it's from Minister Jarnjak on 28th of August. And it talks about, as you can see, the third paragraph -- sorry, if we could change the page in English, please. The third paragraph talks about the needs in the liberated territories concerning numbers of policemen and the problem of the fact that -- it says: "It will not be possible to keep such a large number of policemen as assistants much longer due to structural, economic, and operational reasons and for reasons regarding the assessment of the volume and importance of the jobs and tasks which await us." It says, Therefore, the problem with the formation of police administrations, stations, and substations within the liberated territories is to be dealt with immediately to be resolved by 31 March 1996. Then talks about the police administrations in the liberated areas are to commence the manning of the planned job positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we turn the page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The manning of those police administrations and police stations in the liberated area is to be conducted at a rate of 15 per cent per month. And under number 4 it says: "All other police administrations are to decrease the assistance which they are providing to the administration noted under item 1 at a rate of 15 per cent per month." And if we could look at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we turn the page in English, please. Or if we could scroll down, I'm not sure that if it's -- yes, if we could turn the page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It notes that it is forwarded to the deputy minister and all assistants to the minister. Now, do you recall receiving this specific document from Minister Jarnjak?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: I can't recall specifically, but there would be no reason why I would not -- for me not to receive it, that is. If it has been sent to all assistant ministers, that included myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall a discussion within the OA Povratak action about -- towards the end of August that the police that had been sent in from outside the liberated territories to assist had to be withdrawn gradually, and the police that were now being formed within the liberated area had to start increasing their own personnel in the area? Do you remember a discussion about this?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that 2D00-531 be marked, and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit D1576.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. Before we have a break, Mr. Misetic, I would like to ask one additional question. Mr. Zidovec, could you tell me, what a recruitment to be carried out at a rate of 15 per cent a month means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it involved a process of replacing men who had been in the field for a while and had already been exhausted by the work performed. What it also may have included was that personnel was being transferred from one police administration to the next, and this flow of personnel meant that some police administrations were understaffed. So in my view, this was a rotation of personnel with a view to meeting the needs arising in the liberated area, whilst not disturbing the work in the mother administration, so to speak, in the parent administrations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was what this 15 per cent actually meant. Would it mean to replace 15 per cent of the total force per month? Would it mean that 15 per cent of the force would be considered to be exhausted? Would it be that you would fill 15 per cent of the vacant positions not counting the positions that were filled by others? I'm just trying to understand what does that mean. The 15 per cent, I do see that there was a need to strengthen and to refresh. But what does recruitment of 15 per cent per month mean? 15 per cent of what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't give you a specific answer. This was fully outside of my remit. I simply don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zidovec. We'll have a break, and we will resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two brief matters, Mr. Misetic. The one unrelated to this witness, we announced that the 16th of July was a non-sitting day. Mr. Kehoe asked us to consider whether the 17th, being a non-sitting day would be feasible. We have explored the possibilities; they are non-existent, unfortunately, Mr. Kehoe. So, therefore the 16th. Apart from that, the 20th of July will be a non-sitting day as well. This far, not in relation to the witness, as far as the other document, the tables are concerned, we see that that document starts in the original with a page -- first of all, it starts with one page with an empty stamp which is not translated. However that same stamp. But now filled in - it's a kind of a form - is translated, then we have the order or the -- which we dealt with earlier. What then follows is apparently a list of police administrations which is not translated. Of course, the language is very much the same in repetition, but it is not translated. And that -- I think that if, for example, would you have of all the used terms, [B/C/S spoken], [B/C/S spoken], then that comes back 27 times, but also the -- although we could guess what is the title of it, we would like to have a translation for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that is a list of -- that's three pages. Then we first come to the first table, OA Return Assistance. That page is fully translated. However, on the page after that, in the original, we find in the title the date of the 27th of August, 1995. That is not translated. And what we find there, there are several pages. Sometimes it's same content with some handwriting, and then in an other copy of apparently the same document, the handwriting is replaced by typescript. But we have no -- even not the titles, the columns are not translated. So as it stands now, either are you limited to only the fully translated table, in which at least the incompleteness of translation is not a problem anymore. Whether there are any other problems, that is then still to be seen. So if you want to have everything and then please prepare for a full translation to the extent possible, perhaps discuss with Mr. Carrier whether the objections are still outstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. President, what I had sent around yesterday was the Gotovina Defence's original and translation. I'm content with the Cermak Defence's translation which is already uploaded into e-court and just tendering that into evidence. So I'm interested in the chart, the first chart with the numbers -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the problem is this Court has no access to uploaded documents immediately --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I can call it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you do that, then I can compare that with the document I have in hard copy here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may we have 65 ter 2D00-131 on the screen, please. You see, Mr. President, that the one document you were stating is translated here. And then if we turn to page 2 and then page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that's uploaded in e-court. The third page contains -- I'll check it again. Yes, these are the seven rows in OA Return, help, all fully translated. Yes, it seems all the numbers are all exactly the same. And then we have the other table. Yes, that seems to be a complete translation of everything. I was looking at the numbers, whether they are approximately the same. Yes. Mr. Carrier, you had a similar opportunity to check whether we have everything in translation now. Translation issue seems to be resolved, if we would use this version of the document. I'm -- I must say, not entirely. Not entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: No, that's actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, for example, I see that on --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, let me see --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's what -- I'm talking to my case manager about the numbers in Zadar-Knin don't seem to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you verify, and could you sit together with Mr. Carrier and see whether we have finally -- because if numbers are not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I propose that since the numbers are going to be the same whether they are in the B/C/S or in the English, that they could be verified in the original, and then we will discuss and circulate a final translation to fix any errors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, it seems that not for the full 100 per cent, but for 98 per cent of the problems have been resolved, the technical problems. Any further objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it can be admitted into evidence, but the Chamber would like to receive, let's say, within the next 24 hours whether there is any reason to review whether there are any technical mistakes. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit D1577.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence, with the provisio I just expressed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. While we have this exhibit on the screen, if we could also have the original Croatian version of the chart, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, I just want to see if you can help us perhaps understand the chart. You may or may not be able to help us. It says OA Povratak at the top.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us, having been an assistant minister of the interior, the title is in Croatian "ispomoc," which is help, can you tell us what your understanding would be as to what this chart represents.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: In my view, the chart contains information on additional police forces sent from certain police administrations to other police administrations. The aim was to assess the situation in Sector South and elsewhere, where it was necessary to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the column Zadar-Knin, which is the second column -- second row, I should say. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we could blow that row up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where it says: "First echelon of help," what the entry there means, in your interpretation.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: I think an assessment had to be made of the strength of forces which would be able to cover all the problematic areas. In other words, we simply did not know what the specific --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, could you tell us what you know and what you don't know. It is not always clear whether are you looking at the document and try to understand what it means and then give us your explanation of what it means, or whether have you any knowledge on how this 1st echelon and the 2nd echelon, what it really means. Do you know it, or are you just interpreting, or mainly interpreting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly what the term "echelon" means in this specific case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that was apparently the issue in respect of this table.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please tell us if you do not know, rather tell us than try to digest in your own thoughts what it could mean and then present that as the most likely interpretation of the document. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, at paragraph 45 of your statement, you discuss fire prevention service, and I'd like to ask you a few questions about that. But first let me show you D600. Now, fire prevention was part of your portfolio. And if we look at this document, this is also an OA Povratak order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we scroll down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's the 6th of August. It has your signature and stamp. And it says -- the subject is evidence of fires for the purpose of statistical record of fires that were the result of combat operations in the areas of your police administrations ... it is necessary to send to this headquarters the following information for the previous day." And you see what you instructed the fire services to report. Number 2 is cause of fire. And my question to you is, how would the -- what is your understanding of what the fire service would do to determine the cause of a fire?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: The fire prevention service must know the cause of fire. That's part of its job, to determine whether the fire was caused by a war activity, by someone setting something on fire, or for -- for quite a different reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this. The order says that you're seeking this information to keep statistical records of fires that were the result of combat operations. If -- what would happen in the event that one of the fire teams determined that the cause of the fire was not as a result of combat operations but a deliberate fire set as arson by a member of the military? What would the procedure be, once that cause of fire was established?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: The data on all the fires that were not results of combat activities were sent by fire-fighting units to the criminal police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Which criminal police would they send it to?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: To the criminal police at the seat of the ministry. I assume that the -- they also forwarded this to the relevant police administration in the field, so in Knin or elsewhere, wherever the fire occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me show you a video, Mr. Zidovec, on the basis of that last answer as the foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is Exhibit D508. I believe the transcripts have been provided to the booths.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether that could be the basis for the last answer is -- is still --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... anticipating an objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but it's of course also highly suggestive that here you'll find the basis for your last answer, which is not what I expect you to do, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it wasn't directed to the witness; it was directed to Mr. Carrier. Because I'm trying to find the line whether have I established a foundation or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, the witness hears whatever you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Journalist: Mr. Minister, Jim Rupert, Washington Post. What information does your government have concerning the reports of setting villages on fire by the Bosnian army that entered the Croatian territory to provide support to the Croatian military operation? "Jarnjak: I have no information concerning this matter. However, when we come to that area, and any area, the police will establish the actual state of affairs, inspect each object, take records, and thereupon establish whether it was caused by combat activities or something else. Then I will be able to give a specific answer to your question."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zidovec, is what the minister says there the correct procedure as to how it would be established or who would establish whether a cause -- a fire was caused in combat or as arson by the military?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Given that the order which I signed was sent to a range of police administrations from Vukovar onwards, it is rather difficult for me to answer your question. The fire-fighters could not work in all the areas in the same way. They could not even be in all the areas. However, wherever they there were fire-fighters, obviously they could also establish the causes of fires. From their reports, the crime police could deduce the elements for their further activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. My specific question, though, is whether it was ultimately determined by the fire service that the fire was deliberately caused by civilian or military personnel, would jurisdiction still remain with the crime police to investigate the arson further?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask to you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the first determination of whether a fire was caused by arson or in combat, is determined by the fire service of the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: In the given circumstances where they were present, they could indeed make such an estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what would happen if -- let me change the question. If the cause of the fire was determined to be arson, would it matter whether you suspected, at the fire level, that the arson was set by the military or the civilian police? Or would the fire service report it to the crime police of the MUP, and then they would deal with the issue of who caused the fire?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC
utterances.text: Our reports were sent to the police stations in the field and also to the crime police at the level of the police administration and also at the level of the ministry, which then processed them in their criminal reports when they decided to make -- to file criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
